title.ar: الموضوع ٢ · الدوال والتحويلات (توسعات المستوى العالي HL)

body.en: HL Functions deepens the study of mappings and polynomial theory: piecewise modulus transformations, oblique asymptotes of rational curves, Vieta's symmetric polynomial formulas, and complete factorization over the complex field.
body.ar: HL الدوال deepens the study of mappings and كثيرة الحدود theory: piecewise modulus transformations, oblique خطوط التقارب of rational curves, Vieta's symmetric كثيرة الحدود الصيغ, and complete factorization over the complex field.

label.en: ● Level 1 Foundation — Modulus Function Transformations & Inverses
label.ar: ● Level 1 Foundation — Modulus الدالة Transformations & Inverses

body.en:
The Modulus (Absolute Value) Function: Defined piecewise by: \[ |x| = \begin{cases} x & x \ge 0 \\ -x & x < 0 \end{cases} \] Cartesian Graph Transformations:

  • \(y = |f(x)|\): Reflects any portion of the curve where \(f(x) < 0\) across the \(x\)-axis into the upper half-plane. Output is strictly non-negative (\(y \ge 0\)). Vertices/cusps occur where \(f(x) = 0\).
  • \(y = f(|x|)\): Erases the left half of the graph (\(x < 0\)) and reflects the right half (\(x \ge 0\)) across the \(y\)-axis. The resulting curve has even symmetry: \(f(|{-x}|) = f(|x|)\).

Injectivity & Inverse Functions: An inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) exists if and only if \(f\) is a bijection (one-to-one and onto). For non-injective functions (e.g. parabolas), the domain must be restricted (e.g. \(x \ge h\) where \(h\) is the vertex). The graph of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) is the reflection of \(y = f(x)\) in the line \(y = x\).

Self-Inverse Property: A function is self-inverse if \(f(f(x)) = x\), or \(f^{-1}(x) = f(x)\). For linear rational functions: \[ f(x) = \frac{ax + b}{cx - a} \implies f(f(x)) = x \quad (\text{symmetric about } y = x). \]
body.ar:
The Modulus (Absolute Value) الدالة: Defined piecewise by: \[ |x| = \begin{cases} x & x \ge 0 \\ -x & x < 0 \end{cases} \] Cartesian التمثيل البياني Transformations:

  • \(y = |f(x)|\): Reflects any portion of the curve حيث \(f(x) < 0\) across the \(x\)-axis into the upper half-plane. Output is strictly non-negative (\(y \ge 0\)). Vertices/cusps occur حيث \(f(x) = 0\).
  • \(y = f(|x|)\): Erases the left half of the التمثيل البياني (\(x < 0\)) and reflects the right half (\(x \ge 0\)) across the \(y\)-axis. The resulting curve has even symmetry: \(f(|{-x}|) = f(|x|)\).

Injectivity & Inverse الدوال: An inverse الدالة \(f^{-1}(x)\) exists if and only if \(f\) is a bijection (one-to-one and onto). For non-injective الدوال (e.g. parabolas), the المجال must be restricted (e.g. \(x \ge h\) حيث \(h\) is the الرأس). The التمثيل البياني of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) is the reflection of \(y = f(x)\) in the line \(y = x\).

Self-Inverse Property: A الدالة is self-inverse if \(f(f(x)) = x\), or \(f^{-1}(x) = f(x)\). For linear rational الدوال: \[ f(x) = \frac{ax + b}{cx - a} \implies f(f(x)) = x \quad (\text{symmetric about } y = x). \]

label.en: ▲ Level 2 Analytical Tools — Polynomial Division, Vieta's Relations & Modulus
label.ar: ▲ Level 2 Analytical Tools — كثيرة الحدود Division, Vieta's Relations & Modulus

body.en:
Polynomial Division Algorithm: For any polynomials \(P(x)\) and \(D(x) \neq 0\), there exist unique polynomials \(Q(x)\) and \(R(x)\) such that: \[ P(x) = D(x)Q(x) + R(x), \quad \text{where } \deg(R) < \deg(D). \] Remainder & Factor Theorems:

  • Remainder Theorem: The remainder upon dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x - c)\) is exactly \(P(c)\). If dividing by \((ax - b)\), the remainder is \(P(b/a)\).
  • Factor Theorem: \((x - c)\) is a factor of \(P(x) \iff P(c) = 0\).

Vieta's Formulas (Roots and Coefficients): Let \(P(x) = a_n x^n + a_{n-1}x^{n-1} + \dots + a_1 x + a_0 = 0\) have roots \(\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \dots, \alpha_n \in \mathbb{C}\). Then the elementary symmetric polynomials of the roots satisfy: \[ \sum_{i=1}^n \alpha_i = -\frac{a_{n-1}}{a_n}, \quad \sum_{1 \le i < j \le n} \alpha_i \alpha_j = \frac{a_{n-2}}{a_n}, \quad \dots, \quad \prod_{i=1}^n \alpha_i = (-1)^n \frac{a_0}{a_n}. \] For a cubic \(ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d = 0\) with roots \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\): \[ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = -\frac{b}{a}, \quad \alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha = \frac{c}{a}, \quad \alpha\beta\gamma = -\frac{d}{a}. \] Useful identity for sum of squares of roots: \(\alpha^2 + \beta^2 + \gamma^2 = (\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2 - 2(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)\).

Modulus Inequalities Strategy:

  • \(|f(x)| \le g(x) \iff -g(x) \le f(x) \le g(x)\) (with condition \(g(x) \ge 0\)).
  • \(|f(x)| \ge g(x) \iff f(x) \le -g(x) \text{ or } f(x) \ge g(x)\).
  • \(|f(x)| < |g(x)| \iff [f(x)]^2 < [g(x)]^2 \iff [f(x) - g(x)][f(x) + g(x)] < 0\) (squaring both sides is valid because both sides are non-negative).
body.ar:
Polynomial Division Algorithm: For any polynomials \(P(x)\) and \(D(x) \neq 0\), there exist unique polynomials \(Q(x)\) and \(R(x)\) such that: \[ P(x) = D(x)Q(x) + R(x), \quad \text{where } \deg(R) < \deg(D). \] Remainder & Factor Theorems:

  • Remainder مبرهنة: The remainder upon dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x - c)\) is exactly \(P(c)\). If dividing by \((ax - b)\), the remainder is \(P(b/a)\).
  • Factor مبرهنة: \((x - c)\) is a factor of \(P(x) \iff P(c) = 0\).

Vieta's الصيغ (Roots and المعاملات): Let \(P(x) = a_n x^n + a_{n-1}x^{n-1} + \dots + a_1 x + a_0 = 0\) have roots \(\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \dots, \alpha_n \in \mathbb{C}\). Then the elementary symmetric polynomials of the roots satisfy: \[ \sum_{i=1}^n \alpha_i = -\frac{a_{n-1}}{a_n}, \quad \sum_{1 \le i < j \le n} \alpha_i \alpha_j = \frac{a_{n-2}}{a_n}, \quad \dots, \quad \prod_{i=1}^n \alpha_i = (-1)^n \frac{a_0}{a_n}. \] For a cubic \(ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d = 0\) with roots \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\): \[ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = -\frac{b}{a}, \quad \alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha = \frac{c}{a}, \quad \alpha\beta\gamma = -\frac{d}{a}. \] Useful المتطابقة for sum of squares of roots: \(\alpha^2 + \beta^2 + \gamma^2 = (\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2 - 2(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)\).

Modulus المتباينات Strategy:

  • \(|f(x)| \le g(x) \iff -g(x) \le f(x) \le g(x)\) (with condition \(g(x) \ge 0\)).
  • \(|f(x)| \ge g(x) \iff f(x) \le -g(x) \text{ or } f(x) \ge g(x)\).
  • \(|f(x)| < |g(x)| \iff [f(x)]^2 < [g(x)]^2 \iff [f(x) - g(x)][f(x) + g(x)] < 0\) (squaring both sides is valid because both sides are non-negative).

label.en: ▲ Level 3 University Rigor — Theorem: Rational Asymptotics & Complex Factorization
label.ar: ▲ Level 3 University Rigor — مبرهنة: Rational Asymptotics & Complex Factorization

body.en:
Asymptotics of Rational Functions: Consider the rational function \(R(x) = \frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\) where \(P, Q\) share no common factors:

  • Vertical Asymptotes: Occur at every real zero of \(Q(x)\). Near each root \(x = c\), \(\lim_{x\to c} |R(x)| = \infty\). If \(P(x)\) and \(Q(x)\) share a common factor \((x - c)^k\), cancellation leaves a removable singularity (hole) at \(x = c\) if the multiplicity in \(P\) is \(\ge\) multiplicity in \(Q\).
  • Horizontal Asymptotes: If \(\deg(P) < \deg(Q)\), the \(x\)-axis \(y = 0\) is the horizontal asymptote. If \(\deg(P) = \deg(Q)\), the horizontal asymptote is \(y = \frac{a_n}{b_n}\) (ratio of leading coefficients).
  • Oblique (Slant) Asymptotes: If \(\deg(P) = \deg(Q) + 1\), polynomial long division yields: \[ R(x) = mx + c + \frac{R_0(x)}{Q(x)}, \quad \text{where } \deg(R_0) < \deg(Q). \] Since \(\lim_{x\to\pm\infty} \frac{R_0(x)}{Q(x)} = 0\), the linear function \(y = mx + c\) is an oblique asymptote.
  • Asymptote Crossing: A rational curve can intersect its non-vertical asymptote! Points of intersection with \(y = mx + c\) are determined by solving the remainder equation: \[ R(x) - (mx + c) = 0 \iff R_0(x) = 0. \]
  • Range via Quadratic Discriminant: To find the range of \(y = \frac{ax^2+bx+c}{dx^2+ex+f}\), rearrange into a quadratic in \(x\): \((yd - a)x^2 + (ye - b)x + (yf - c) = 0\). For real \(x\) to exist, the discriminant must satisfy \(\Delta(y) = [ye - b]^2 - 4(yd - a)(yf - c) \ge 0\). The resulting polynomial inequality determines the exact range of \(y\).
body.ar:
Asymptotics of Rational الدوال: Consider the rational الدالة \(R(x) = \frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\) حيث \(P, Q\) share no common factors:

  • Vertical خطوط التقارب: Occur at every real zero of \(Q(x)\). Near each root \(x = c\), \(\lim_{x\to c} |R(x)| = \infty\). If \(P(x)\) and \(Q(x)\) share a common factor \((x - c)^k\), cancellation leaves a removable singularity (hole) at \(x = c\) if the multiplicity in \(P\) is \(\ge\) multiplicity in \(Q\).
  • Horizontal خطوط التقارب: If \(\deg(P) < \deg(Q)\), the \(x\)-axis \(y = 0\) is the horizontal خط التقارب. If \(\deg(P) = \deg(Q)\), the horizontal خط التقارب is \(y = \frac{a_n}{b_n}\) (ratio of leading المعاملات).
  • Oblique (Slant) خطوط التقارب: If \(\deg(P) = \deg(Q) + 1\), كثيرة الحدود long division yields: \[ R(x) = mx + c + \frac{R_0(x)}{Q(x)}, \quad \text{where } \deg(R_0) < \deg(Q). \] Since \(\lim_{x\to\pm\infty} \frac{R_0(x)}{Q(x)} = 0\), the linear الدالة \(y = mx + c\) is an oblique asymptote.
  • Asymptote Crossing: A rational curve can intersect its non-vertical خط التقارب! Points of التقاطع with \(y = mx + c\) are determined by solving the remainder المعادلة: \[ R(x) - (mx + c) = 0 \iff R_0(x) = 0. \]
  • Range via Quadratic Discriminant: To أوجد مدى \(y = \frac{ax^2+bx+c}{dx^2+ex+f}\), rearrange into a quadratic in \(x\): \((yd - a)x^2 + (ye - b)x + (yf - c) = 0\). For real \(x\) to exist, the discriminant must satisfy \(\Delta(y) = [ye - b]^2 - 4(yd - a)(yf - c) \ge 0\). The resulting كثيرة الحدود المتباينة determines the exact المدى of \(y\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Functions (HL Extensions))
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (الدوال (HL Extensions))

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the المدى to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

label.en: Worked Example 2.1 — Analytical Solution of Modulus Equation
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.1 — Analytical الحل of Modulus المعادلة

problem.ar: مسألة تطبيقية: Sketch \(y = |2x - 4|\) and algebraically solve \(|2x - 4| = x + 1\).

solution.en:
1. Geometric sketch: \(y = |2x - 4|\) is a V-shaped curve with vertex at \((2, 0)\), \(y\)-intercept at \((0, 4)\), and rays \(y = 2x - 4\) for \(x \ge 2\) and \(y = -(2x - 4) = 4 - 2x\) for \(x < 2\).

2. Pre-condition: \(|2x - 4| \ge 0 \implies x + 1 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -1\).

3. Case 1 (\(x \ge 2\)):
\[ 2x - 4 = x + 1 \implies x = 5. \] Check: \(5 \ge 2\), and \(|2(5) - 4| = 6 = 5 + 1\). Valid! ✓

4. Case 2 (\(x < 2\)):
\[ -(2x - 4) = x + 1 \implies 4 - 2x = x + 1 \implies 3x = 3 \implies x = 1. \] Check: \(1 < 2\), and \(|2(1) - 4| = |-2| = 2 = 1 + 1\). Valid! ✓

Solutions: \(x = 1\) and \(x = 5\).
solution.ar:
1. Geometric sketch: \(y = |2x - 4|\) is a V-shaped curve with الرأس at \((2, 0)\), \(y\)-المقطع at \((0, 4)\), and rays \(y = 2x - 4\) for \(x \ge 2\) and \(y = -(2x - 4) = 4 - 2x\) for \(x < 2\).

2. Pre-condition: \(|2x - 4| \ge 0 \implies x + 1 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -1\).

3. Case 1 (\(x \ge 2\)):
\[ 2x - 4 = x + 1 \implies x = 5. \] Check: \(5 \ge 2\), and \(|2(5) - 4| = 6 = 5 + 1\). Valid! ✓

4. Case 2 (\(x < 2\)):
\[ -(2x - 4) = x + 1 \implies 4 - 2x = x + 1 \implies 3x = 3 \implies x = 1. \] Check: \(1 < 2\), and \(|2(1) - 4| = |-2| = 2 = 1 + 1\). Valid! ✓

Solutions: \(x = 1\) and \(x = 5\).

label.en: Worked Example 2.2 — Complex Factorization & Vieta Verification
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.2 — Complex Factorization & Vieta Verification

problem.en: Given that \(p(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 7x - 5\) has a root \(x = 1\), find all roots and verify Vieta's formulas.
problem.ar: بما أن \(p(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 7x - 5\) has a root \(x = 1\), find all roots and verify Vieta's الصيغ.

solution.en:
1. Since \(x = 1\) is a root, \((x - 1)\) is a factor. Perform synthetic or polynomial division: \[ x^3 - 3x^2 + 7x - 5 = (x - 1)(x^2 - 2x + 5). \] 2. Find the roots of the quadratic factor \(x^2 - 2x + 5 = 0\): \[ x = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{(-2)^2 - 4(1)(5)}}{2} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 20}}{2} = \frac{2 \pm 4i}{2} = 1 \pm 2i. \] Thus the three roots are \(\alpha = 1\), \(\beta = 1 + 2i\), \(\gamma = 1 - 2i\).

3. Verify Vieta's Formulas:
Sum of roots: \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 1 + (1+2i) + (1-2i) = 3 = -\frac{-3}{1}\). ✓
Sum of pairwise products: \[ \alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha = 1(1+2i) + (1+2i)(1-2i) + 1(1-2i) = (1+2i) + (1+4) + (1-2i) = 7 = \frac{7}{1}. \quad \checkmark \] Product of roots: \[ \alpha\beta\gamma = 1(1+4) = 5 = -\frac{-5}{1}. \quad \checkmark \]
solution.ar:
1. Since \(x = 1\) is a root, \((x - 1)\) is a factor. Perform synthetic or كثيرة الحدود division: \[ x^3 - 3x^2 + 7x - 5 = (x - 1)(x^2 - 2x + 5). \] 2. أوجد roots of the quadratic factor \(x^2 - 2x + 5 = 0\): \[ x = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{(-2)^2 - 4(1)(5)}}{2} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 20}}{2} = \frac{2 \pm 4i}{2} = 1 \pm 2i. \] وعليه the three roots are \(\alpha = 1\), \(\beta = 1 + 2i\), \(\gamma = 1 - 2i\).

3. Verify Vieta's الصيغ:
Sum of roots: \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 1 + (1+2i) + (1-2i) = 3 = -\frac{-3}{1}\). ✓
Sum of pairwise products: \[ \alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha = 1(1+2i) + (1+2i)(1-2i) + 1(1-2i) = (1+2i) + (1+4) + (1-2i) = 7 = \frac{7}{1}. \quad \checkmark \] Product of roots: \[ \alpha\beta\gamma = 1(1+4) = 5 = -\frac{-5}{1}. \quad \checkmark \]

label.en: Worked Example 2.3 — Oblique Asymptote of Rational Function
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.3 — Oblique خط التقارب of Rational الدالة

problem.en: Find the oblique asymptote of \(f(x) = \dfrac{2x^2 + 3x - 1}{x - 1}\) and determine whether the curve intersects it.
problem.ar: أوجد oblique خط التقارب of \(f(x) = \dfrac{2x^2 + 3x - 1}{x - 1}\) and حدّد ما إذا كان the curve intersects it.

solution.en:
1. Divide \(2x^2 + 3x - 1\) by \(x - 1\) using polynomial long division: \[ \begin{array}{r} 2x + 5 \quad \\ x - 1 {\overline{\smash{\big)}\,2x^2 + 3x - 1}} \\ \underline{-(2x^2 - 2x)} \phantom{-1} \\ 5x - 1 \\ \underline{-(5x - 5)} \\ 4 \end{array} \] 2. Express \(f(x)\) in quotient-remainder form: \[ f(x) = 2x + 5 + \frac{4}{x - 1}. \] 3. As \(x \to \pm\infty\), \(\frac{4}{x - 1} \to 0\). Therefore, the oblique asymptote is \(y = 2x + 5\).

4. Check for intersection: set \(f(x) = 2x + 5\): \[ 2x + 5 + \frac{4}{x - 1} = 2x + 5 \implies \frac{4}{x - 1} = 0. \] Since \(\frac{4}{x - 1} \neq 0\) for any real \(x\), the curve never intersects its oblique asymptote.
solution.ar:
1. Divide \(2x^2 + 3x - 1\) by \(x - 1\) using كثيرة الحدود long division: \[ \begin{array}{r} 2x + 5 \quad \\ x - 1 {\overline{\smash{\big)}\,2x^2 + 3x - 1}} \\ \underline{-(2x^2 - 2x)} \phantom{-1} \\ 5x - 1 \\ \underline{-(5x - 5)} \\ 4 \end{array} \] 2. Express \(f(x)\) in quotient-remainder form: \[ f(x) = 2x + 5 + \frac{4}{x - 1}. \] 3. As \(x \to \pm\infty\), \(\frac{4}{x - 1} \to 0\). وبالتالي, the oblique خط التقارب is \(y = 2x + 5\).

4. Check for التقاطع: set \(f(x) = 2x + 5\): \[ 2x + 5 + \frac{4}{x - 1} = 2x + 5 \implies \frac{4}{x - 1} = 0. \] Since \(\frac{4}{x - 1} \neq 0\) for any real \(x\), the curve never intersects its oblique asymptote.

label.en: ⚠ Topic 2 Exam Traps: Modulus & Inverse Functions
label.ar: ⚠ Topic 2 Exam Traps: Modulus & Inverse الدوال

body.en:
Squaring Modulus Equations: While squaring both sides of \(|ax+b| = |cx+d|\) is convenient, squaring when one side is variable without modulus (e.g. \(|2x-3| = x-1\)) can introduce extraneous roots. Always check candidates in the un-squared equation.

Self-Inverse Functions: For rational functions of the form \(f(x) = \dfrac{ax+b}{cx-a}\), \(f(x) = f^{-1}(x)\). Recognize this symmetry immediately to save algebraic time.

Domain Restrictions on Inverses: For quadratic functions, an inverse function only exists if the domain is restricted to one side of the vertex (e.g. \(x \ge h\)). Stating \(f^{-1}\) without stating its restricted domain \(x \ge k\) loses marks.
body.ar:
Squaring Modulus المعادلات: While squaring both sides of \(|ax+b| = |cx+d|\) is convenient, squaring عندما one side is المتغير without modulus (e.g. \(|2x-3| = x-1\)) can introduce extraneous roots. Always check candidates in the un-squared المعادلة.

Self-Inverse الدوال: For rational الدوال of the form \(f(x) = \dfrac{ax+b}{cx-a}\), \(f(x) = f^{-1}(x)\). Recognize this symmetry immediately to save algebraic time.

Domain Restrictions on Inverses: For quadratic الدوال, an inverse الدالة only exists if the المجال is restricted to one side of the الرأس (e.g. \(x \ge h\)). Stating \(f^{-1}\) without stating its restricted المجال \(x \ge k\) loses marks.

Always check if \(f(x) = mx + k\) has finite solutions.
AHL 2.14–2.16 Odd/Even, \(|f(x)|\), \(f(|x|)\) & \(1/f(x)\)Sketching \(y = |f(x)|\), \(y = f(|x|)\), and \(y = 1/f(x)\) on the same axes; solving \(|2x - 3| < |x + 1|\) algebraically or graphically.For \(y = f(|x|)\), forgetting to erase the original left-hand branch (\(x < 0\)) before reflecting the \(x \ge 0\) branch across the \(y\)-axis.

Worked Example (AA HL Paper 1 — 8 marks):
Consider \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 - 3x + 6}{x - 1}\) for \(x \ne 1\).
(a) Express \(f(x)\) in the form \(x + a + \frac{b}{x - 1}\) and hence state the equation of the oblique asymptote. [3]
(b) Find the coordinates of the local maximum and local minimum points on the graph of \(f\), and hence state the range of \(f\). [5]

Official IB Markscheme Solution:
(a) \(x^2 - 3x + 6 = (x - 1)(x - 2) + 4 \implies f(x) = x - 2 + \frac{4}{x - 1}\) (\(a = -2, b = 4\)) [M1] [A1]
Oblique asymptote is \(y = x - 2\) [A1]
(b) \(f'(x) = 1 - \frac{4}{(x-1)^2} = 0 \implies (x-1)^2 = 4 \implies x - 1 = \pm 2 \implies x = 3\) or \(x = -1\) [M1] [A1]
At \(x = -1\), \(f(-1) = -1 - 2 - 2 = -5\) (Local Max \((-1, -5)\)); at \(x = 3\), \(f(3) = 3 - 2 + 2 = 3\) (Local Min \((3, 3)\)) [A1] [A1]
Range of \(f\): \((-\infty, -5] \cup [3, \infty)\) (or \(y \le -5\) or \(y \ge 3\)) [A1]

question.en: Find the exact range of \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{x^2 + 1}\) for \(x \in \mathbb{R}\).

solution.en:
Let \(y = \frac{x}{x^2 + 1}\). Multiply both sides by \(x^2 + 1\) (valid since \(x^2 + 1 > 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\)): \[ y(x^2 + 1) = x \implies yx^2 - x + y = 0. \] If \(y = 0\), \(-x = 0 \implies x = 0\), so \(0\) is in the range.
For \(y eq 0\), this is a quadratic equation in \(x\). For real \(x\) to exist, the discriminant \(\Delta\) must be non-negative: \[ \Delta = (-1)^2 - 4(y)(y) = 1 - 4y^2 \ge 0. \] Solve the inequality: \[ 4y^2 \le 1 \implies y^2 \le \frac{1}{4} \implies -\frac{1}{2} \le y \le \frac{1}{2}. \] Thus the range of \(f(x)\) is \(\left[-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right]\).
solution.ar:

question.en: [Practice 2 · Medium] The graph of the function \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 - ax + 6}{x-1}\) is shown below. The graph has a vertical asymptote at \(x=1\) and a point of discontinuity at \((2, k)\). Find the value of \(a\).
question.ar: [Practice 2 · Medium] The graph of the function \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 - ax + 6}{x-1}\) is shown below. The graph has a vertical asymptote at \(x=1\) and a point of discontinuity at \((2, k)\). أوجد قيمة \(a\).

hints.en: The function is given by \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 - ax + 6}{x-1}\). \(x=1\) is a vertical asymptote, which means that \(x-1\) is not a factor of the numerator, and when \(x=1\), the numerator is non-zero. The point of discontinuity is at \((2, k)\). This implies that \(x=2\) is a root of the numerator, so \(f(2)=0\) or the expression is undefined at \(x=2\) if \(x-2\) were a factor of the denominator. Since the denominator is \(x-1\), which is not zero at \(x=2\), the function must be zero at \(x=2\) for there to be a removable discontinuity (a hole). Therefore, the numerator must be zero when \(x=2\).
hints.ar: The function is given by \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 - ax + 6}{x-1}\). \(x=1\) is a vertical asymptote, which means that \(x-1\) is not a حلّل of the numerator, and عندما \(x=1\), the numerator is non-zero. The point of discontinuity is at \((2, k)\). This implies that \(x=2\) is a root of the numerator, so \(f(2)=0\) or the expression is undefined at \(x=2\) إذا كان \(x-2\) were a حلّل of the denominator. Since the denominator is \(x-1\), which is not zero at \(x=2\), the function must be zero at \(x=2\) for there to be a removable discontinuity (a hole). وبالتالي، the numerator must be zero عندما \(x=2\).

hints.en: Use the resulting form to finish: \(10 - 2a\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(10 - 2a\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en: The function is given by \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 - ax + 6}{x-1}\). \(x=1\) is a vertical asymptote, which means that \(x-1\) is not a factor of the numerator, and when \(x=1\), the numerator is non-zero. The point of discontinuity is at \((2, k)\). This implies that \(x=2\) is a root of the numerator, so \(f(2)=0\) or the expression is undefined at \(x=2\) if \(x-2\) were a factor of the denominator. Since the denominator is \(x-1\), which is not zero at \(x=2\), the function must be zero at \(x=2\) for there to be a removable discontinuity (a hole). Therefore, the numerator must be zero when \(x=2\). Substitute \(x=2\) into the numerator: \(2^2 - a(2) + 6 = 0\). \(4 - 2a + 6 = 0\). \(10 - 2a = 0\). \(2a = 10\). \(a = 5\). Common algebraic trap: If one incorrectly assumes \(x=2\) is a root of the denominator, it would lead to an incorrect calculation. Also, one might confuse a vertical asymptote with a removable discontinuity.

question.en: [Practice 3 · Medium] The diagram shows the graph of the function \( y = f(x) \). The function is defined by \( f(x) = x^2 + bx + c \). The graph passes through the point \( (1, 0) \) and has a vertex at \( (2, -1) \). Find the value of \( b \).
question.ar: [Practice 3 · Medium] The diagram shows the graph of the function \( y = f(x) \). The function is defined by \( f(x) = x^2 + bx + c \). The graph يمر بالنقطة the point \( (1, 0) \) and has a vertex at \( (2, -1) \). أوجد قيمة \( b \).

hints.en: The vertex of a parabola given by the equation \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \) is at \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \).
hints.ar: The vertex of a parabola given بتطبيق equation \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \) is at \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \).

hints.en: In this case, \( a = 1 \). The vertex is given as \( (2, -1) \), so the x-coordinate of the vertex is 2.
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( a = 1 \) ، \( (2, -1) \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Comparing this with \(y = x^2 + bx + c\), we find \(b = -4\) and \(c\).
hints.ar: Comparing this with \(y = x^2 + bx + c\), we أوجد \(b = -4\) and \(c\).

solution.en: The vertex of a parabola given by the equation \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \) is at \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \). In this case, \( a = 1 \). The vertex is given as \( (2, -1) \), so the x-coordinate of the vertex is 2. Therefore, \( 2 = -\frac{b}{2(1)} \), which implies \( 2 = -\frac{b}{2} \). Multiplying both sides by 2 gives \( 4 = -b \), so \( b = -4 \). Alternatively, using the vertex form of the quadratic equation, \( y = a(x-h)^2 + k \), where \( (h, k) \) is the vertex. Here, \( a=1 \), \( h=2 \), and \( k=-1 \). So, \( y = (x-2)^2 - 1 \). Expanding this, we get \( y = (x^2 - 4x + 4) - 1 \), which simplifies to \( y = x^2 - 4x + 3 \). Comparing this with \( y = x^2 + bx + c \), we find \( b = -4 \) and \( c = 3 \).

The vertex is given as \( (2, -1) \), so the x-coordinate of the vertex is 2. وبالتالي، \( 2 = -\frac{b}{2(1)} \), which implies \( 2 = -\frac{b}{2} \). Multiplying both sides by 2 gives \( 4 = -b \), so \( b = -4 \). Alternatively, باستخدام vertex form of the quadratic equation, \( y = a(x-h)^2 + k \), حيث \( (h, k) \) is the vertex. Here, \( a=1 \), \( h=2 \), and \( k=-1 \). So, \( y = (x-2)^2 - 1 \). فكّ المقدارing this, we get \( y = (x^2 - 4x + 4) - 1 \), which simplإذا كانies to \( y = x^2 - 4x + 3 \). Comparing this with \( y = x^2 + bx + c \), we أوجد \( b = -4 \) and \( c = 3 \).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] The diagram shows the graph of the quadratic function \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx - 2 \). The graph passes through the points \( (1, -3) \) and \( (2, 2) \). Determine the value of \( a \).
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Medium] The diagram shows the graph of the quadratic function \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx - 2 \). The graph يمر بالنقطة the points \( (1, -3) \) and \( (2, 2) \). حدّد value of \( a \).

hints.en: The function is given by \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx - 2 \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx - 2 \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Since the graph passes through \( (1, -3) \), we have \( f(1) = -3 \): \( a(1)^2 + b(1) - 2 = -3 \) \( a + b - 2 = -3 \).
hints.ar: Since the graph يمر بالنقطة \( (1, -3) \), we have \( f(1) = -3 \): \( a(1)^2 + b(1) - 2 = -3 \) \( a + b - 2 = -3 \).

hints.en: Thus, the function is \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 4x - 2\). The value of \(a\) is 3.
hints.ar: وعليه، the function is \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 4x - 2\). The value of \(a\) is 3.

solution.en: The function is given by \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx - 2 \). Since the graph passes through \( (1, -3) \), we have \( f(1) = -3 \): \( a(1)^2 + b(1) - 2 = -3 \) \( a + b - 2 = -3 \) \( a + b = -1 \) (Equation 1) Since the graph passes through \( (2, 2) \), we have \( f(2) = 2 \): \( a(2)^2 + b(2) - 2 = 2 \) \( 4a + 2b - 2 = 2 \) \( 4a + 2b = 4 \) \( 2a + b = 2 \) (Equation 2) Now we solve the system of linear equations for \( a \) and \( b \). Subtract Equation 1 from Equation 2: \( (2a + b) - (a + b) = 2 - (-1) \) \( a = 3 \) Substitute \( a = 3 \) into Equation 1: \( 3 + b = -1 \) \( b = -4 \) Thus, the function is \( f(x) = 3x^2 - 4x - 2 \). The value of \( a \) is 3.
solution.ar: The function is given by \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx - 2 \). Since the graph يمر بالنقطة \( (1, -3) \), we have \( f(1) = -3 \): \( a(1)^2 + b(1) - 2 = -3 \) \( a + b - 2 = -3 \) \( a + b = -1 \) (Equation 1) Since the graph يمر بالنقطة \( (2, 2) \), we have \( f(2) = 2 \): \( a(2)^2 + b(2) - 2 = 2 \) \( 4a + 2b - 2 = 2 \) \( 4a + 2b = 4 \) \( 2a + b = 2 \) (Equation 2) Now we حل النظام of linear equations for \( a \) and \( b \). Subtract Equation 1 from Equation 2: \( (2a + b) - (a + b) = 2 - (-1) \) \( a = 3 \) عوّض \( a = 3 \) into Equation 1: \( 3 + b = -1 \) \( b = -4 \) وعليه، the function is \( f(x) = 3x^2 - 4x - 2 \). The value of \( a \) is 3.

question.en: Determine the equation of the oblique asymptote to the graph of \( f(x) = \frac{2x^2 - 3x + 4}{x - 1} \).
question.ar: حدّد equation of the oblique asymptote to the graph of \( f(x) = \frac{2x^2 - 3x + 4}{x - 1} \).

hints.en: To find the equation of the oblique asymptote, divide the numerator by the denominator using polynomial long division or synthetic division: \(2x^2 - 3x + 4 = 2x(x - 1) - x + 4 = 2x(x - 1) - (x - 1) + 3 = (2x - 1)(x - 1) + 3\).
hints.ar: To أوجد equation of the oblique asymptote, divide the numerator بتطبيق denominator using polynomial long division or synthetic division: \(2x^2 - 3x + 4 = 2x(x - 1) - x + 4 = 2x(x - 1) - (x - 1) + 3 = (2x - 1)(x - 1) + 3\).

hints.en: Dividing through by \( x - 1 \) yields: \(f(x) = 2x - 1 + \frac{3}{x - 1}\) As \( x \to \pm\infty \), the remainder term \( \frac{3}{x - 1} \to 0 \). Therefore, the linear quotient gives the oblique asymptote: \(y = 2x - 1\).

solution.en: To find the equation of the oblique asymptote, divide the numerator by the denominator using polynomial long division or synthetic division: \[ \begin{aligned} 2x^2 - 3x + 4 &= 2x(x - 1) - x + 4 \\ &= 2x(x - 1) - (x - 1) + 3 \\ &= (2x - 1)(x - 1) + 3 \end{aligned} \] Dividing through by \( x - 1 \) yields: \[ f(x) = 2x - 1 + \frac{3}{x - 1} \] As \( x \to \pm\infty \), the remainder term \( \frac{3}{x - 1} \to 0 \). Therefore, the linear quotient gives the oblique asymptote: \[ y = 2x - 1 \] - \( y = 2x - 3 \) arises from mistakenly dividing each of the first two terms by \( x \) directly without performing proper polynomial division. - \( y = 2x + 1 \) arises from a sign error when subtracting \( -2x \) during the division step.
